questions.question: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. The carpenter used a plane to smooth the surface of the wood.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.

The carpenter used a plane to smooth the surface of the wood.
questions.solution:
The underlined phrase is contextually and grammatically correct. The word 'plane' means a tool consisting of a block with a projecting steel blade, used to smooth a wooden or other surface by paring shavings from it. So, the phrase requires no replacement.

Hence, the correct answer is option (d).

questions.question: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. She complemented her friend on how well the dress complemented her figure.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.

She complemented her friend on how well the dress complemented her figure.
questions.solution:
The word "complemented" means contribute extra features to (someone or something) in such a way as to improve or emphasize their qualities. Its use in the underlined phrase is contextually incorrect because the person is appreciating the friend's dress. So, the appropriate word for the context is 'complimented' (politely congratulate or praise (someone) for something). The grammatically correct replacement for the phrase is given in option (b) 'She complimented'.

Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

Note: Option a) is incorrect as the plural verb "compliment" cannot be used for the singular subject "she". Following the past tense structure of the sentence, "complimented" is appropriate.

questions.question: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. The chef needed the dough to make bread fluffy and soft.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.

The chef needed the dough to make bread fluffy and soft.
questions.solution:
The word 'needed' in the sentence is contextually incorrect because 'needed' means require (something) because it is essential or very important rather than just desirable whereas the chef wanted to make the dough soft for which 'kneaded' (work (moistened flour or clay) into dough or paste with the hands) will be the appropriate word. So, the correct replacement for the underlined phrase is given in option (c), 'kneaded the dough'.

Options a) and b) are incorrect as they use the contextually inappropriate words 'needing' and 'need'.

Hence, the correct answer is option (c).

questions.question: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. The wind blew the sale as the boat glided across the sea.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.

The wind blew the sale as the boat glided across the sea.
questions.solution:
In the underlined phrase, the word 'sale' (which means 'the exchange of a commodity for money; the action of selling something') is contextually incorrect. The appropriate word that matches the content of the sentence is 'sail' which means a piece of material extended on a mast to catch the wind and propel a boat or ship or another vessel.

Among the options, 'blew the sail' is the correct replacement for the underlined phrase. Option (b) also uses the word "sale" incorrectly. Option (c) is grammatically incorrect as the plural verb "blow" cannot be used for the singular subject "wind". Following the past tense structure of the sentence, "blew" is the appropriate verb here.

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

Hence, the correct answer is option (d).

questions.question: In the question given below, four statements are given which may or may not contain an error. Choose the one that is grammatically and meaningfully correct.
questions.questionHtml: In the question given below, four statements are given which may or may not contain an error. Choose the one that is grammatically and meaningfully correct.

options.text: I need too apples from the market.
options.html: I need too apples from the market.

options.text: She gave the gift to her sister two.
options.html: She gave the gift to her sister two.

options.text: The children ate two ice creams each.
options.html: The children ate two ice creams each.

options.text: They went two the movie after lunch.
options.html: They went two the movie after lunch.

questions.solution:
Among the given sentences, only sentence c) is error-free.

In sentence (a), the adverb 'too' is used in place of the number 'two'. The correct sentence should be: I need two apples from the market.

In sentence (b), the number 'two' is used in place of adverb 'too'. The correct sentence should be: She gave the gift to her sister too.

In sentence (d), the number 'two' is incorrectly used in the place of 'to'. The correct sentence should be: They went to the movie after lunch.

So, they are negated.

Hence, the correct answer is option (c).

options.html: The baker ran out of flower to bake the cake.

questions.solution:
Among the given sentences, only sentence c) is error free.

In sentences (a) and (b), the noun 'flour' (a powder obtained by grinding grain, typically wheat, and used to make bread, cakes, and pastry) is used in place of the noun 'flower' (the seed-bearing part of a plant, consisting of reproductive organs (stamens and carpels) that are typically surrounded by a brightly coloured corolla (petals) and a green calyx (sepals)) and vice versa for option (d).

So, they are negated.

Hence, the correct answer is option (c).

questions.question: In the question given below, four statements are given which may or may not contain an error. Choose the one that is grammatically and meaningfully correct.
questions.questionHtml: In the question given below, four statements are given which may or may not contain an error. Choose the one that is grammatically and meaningfully correct.

options.text: The captain steered the ship across the sea.
options.html: The captain steered the ship across the sea.

options.text: I want to sea the beautiful views of the coast.
options.html: I want to sea the beautiful views of the coast.

options.text: Turn the light on so I can sea.
options.html: Turn the light on so I can sea.

options.text: I couldn't believe my eyes when I saw a see.
options.html: I couldn't believe my eyes when I saw a see.

questions.solution:
Among the given sentences, only sentence a) is error free.

Sentence b): The verb "see" should be used after the infinitive marker "to", instead of the noun "sea".

Sentence c): The modal verb "can" should be followed by the base verb "see", instead of the noun "sea".

Sentence d): The indefinite article "a" is always followed by the noun. So, the verb "see" should be replaced by the noun "sea".

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

Note:

An infinitive marker is a word or affix that indicates that a verb is in its infinitive form. The most common infinitive marker is "to", which is used before the base form of a verb. For example, "to make" is an infinitive with the infinitive marker "to".

questions.question: Which of the following words can fill in the blank A?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following words can fill in the blank A?
questions.solution:
Blank A requires a noun to indicate the place where John wanted to take a walk. Among the options 'sea' (the expanse of salt water that covers most of the earth's surface and surrounds its land masses) is the only suitable word, which is a noun and can fill in the blank A.

See, seen- Verbs;

Seal (noun/verb)- a substance that is used to join two things together so as to prevent them from coming apart or to prevent anything from passing between them/ fasten or close securely (fails to fit in contextually).

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

questions.question: Which of the following words can fill in the blank B?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following words can fill in the blank B?
questions.solution:
'Pour' is the most appropriate word for blank B because when it is used in the blank it forms a phrasal verb 'pour on' which means to produce a lot of (something) in order to achieve something. This matches the context of the sentence as it can be noted that John wanted to meet his friend, and they are about to start a project for which ideas are required.

"Pours" [third-person singular verb] is grammatically incorrect as "would" [modal verb] needs to be followed by the base verb only.

So, the remaining words are negated as they are contextually irrelevant to the given sentence.

Pore- a very small hole in the skin of people or other animals

Poor- lacking sufficient money to live at a standard considered comfortable or normal in a society.

Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

Note:

Modal verbs show possibility, intent, ability, or necessity. Common examples of modal verbs include can, should, and must. Because they're a type of auxiliary verb (helper verb), they're used alongside the infinitive form of the main verb of a sentence.

questions.question: Which of the following words can fill in the blank C?

These words are contextually unfit for the sentence which talks about a food item for dinner so, they are negated.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank(s). As the sun set, they prepared for the ___ ahead, knowing that a brave ___ would join them in the battle at dawn.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank(s).

As the sun set, they prepared for the ___ ahead, knowing that a brave ___ would join them in the battle at dawn.
questions.solution:
The word that fits the first blank is 'night' because it denotes the time period of the day and the second blank requires a noun that denotes a thing or a person (and is appropriately modified by the adjective "brave") and the suitable word is 'knight'. Accordingly, the option that has the correct order of the words is (a).

Night- The period from sunset to sunrise every twenty-four hours.

Knight- A man who served his sovereign or lord as a mounted soldier in armour.

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank(s). After eating the ______ pizza, he realized there was a ___ in the box.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank(s).

After eating the ______ pizza, he realized there was a ___ in the box.
questions.solution:
The word that fits the first blank is 'whole' because it denotes the quantity that was eaten and the second blank requires a noun that denotes something that is present in the box, once the pizza is eaten, and the suitable word is 'hole'. Accordingly, the option that has the correct order of the words is (a).

Whole- all of; entire.

Hole- a hollow place in a solid body or surface.

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).
